📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-05-28-mobile-asyncstorage-securestore-keychain`
This is occurrence #26 (prior last_seen 2026-08-20T15:39:33Z, ~11 days quiet gap).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Admin` (`@admin` / `#team-admin`)
Playbook: 1) Confirm volume + app version in ES: level:(ERROR OR FATAL) AND fields.dd_service:"nonprod/apps" AND message:"Failed to migrate from AsyncStorage" -- check fields.UserAgent for app version (e.g. Method/2.1.537) and OS (CFNetwork/Darwin = iOS). 2) This is a CLIENT bug: route to the mobile team. Likely cause is a missing/incorrect iOS keychain access group or entitlement, or a SecureStore key collision, introduced by the storage-migration code path in the suspected release (2.1.537). 3) Mitigation options for mobile team: ship a patch that wraps the migration in a try/catch and falls back to AsyncStorage (do not block app start on keychain), or fix the keychain entitlement. 4) Server side: no action beyond monitoring volume; consider whether the /apps/v1/logging/mobile pipeline should down-rank this to WARN to avoid error-tracking noise.
Open Jira: none on file

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-05-21-gateway-microservices-timeout`
This is occurrence #750 in the last 7 days.
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Admin` (`@admin` / `#team-admin`)
Playbook: 1) Confirm chronic baseline by comparing ES Ocelot.Responder.Middleware Warning volume in the alert window vs the same window 24h ago — if delta < 20%, it's the chronic pattern (no new incident). 2) Aggregate timeouts by RequestPath: if dominant paths are all under upstream microservices.methodlocal.int, it's pool-level. 3) Check ki-dns-microservices-method-int-pps-quota first — DNS bursts on the Windows fleet present here as Ocelot timeouts. 4) If DNS is clean: identify which downstream microservice owns the slow path via Ocelot config in ms-gateway-api/gateway/API/ocelot.*.json. 5) Decision tree for the fix: (a) raise per-route Ocelot timeout (cheap, masks symptom), (b) scale microservices IIS pool / shorten recycle interval, (c) profile the upstream microservice under prod load (root-cause fix, expensive).
Open Jira: n/a — no fix_jira on this entry

  • Root-cause-analysis: ES aggregate ("Unusual number of XHR errors for account" OR "monitors/77419271" OR GetSyncWidgetInfoAsync) 15:50:11-16:10:11 UTC = 801 hits, 100% service:gateway, vs 7 hits in the identical window 24h ago (~114.4x). Confirmed at the wider 1h window too (2398 vs 21, ~114.2x) — not a rollup artifact. Sample records show the canonical mechanism: RequestTimedOutError -> TaskCanceledException -> HttpIOException/SocketException(125) -> Ocelot.Responder.Middleware.ResponderMiddleware, RequestPath /syncutil/syncwidget/{account}/GetSyncWidgetInfoAsync. DD XHR log sample (100 records, same window): top account stlouismo2 9% — diffuse, no single-account concentration, matches the documented chronic platform-wide shape (not the 2026-06-04-style outage surge).
  • This-window concentration: gateway 801 (100%)
  • Trend flag: this is the 6th consecutive poll cycle today showing an elevated magnitude for this entry, and the trend is accelerating rather than subsiding — 32-48x -> ~33x -> ~95-112x -> ~92.7x -> ~114.4x this cycle. Worth a human look at whether the chronic baseline itself has shifted.
